text:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: CRITICAL: High 5xx error rate detected for service inference-gateway on prod (threshold 1.5% -> 12.3%). Pager: oncall-sre. Link: https://monitoring.redwood.example/alerts/1762901234

incident-bot: Incident thread created: #INC-2026-042. Page dispatched to oncall-sre, escalation policy 'sre-major'.

alex: acked. I'm oncall, taking lead. First pass: is the spike global or region-specific?

maria: seeing higher 5xxs concentrated on us-east-1 and eu-west-1, same endpoint /v1/generate, mostly short traces around token generation.

samir: adding context: we rolled model-serving 3.2.1 -> 3.2.2 yesterday; autoscaler tweak also shipped. Could be related.

alex: quick checklist: tail gateway logs, check model-serving pods, check autoscaler, check redis/cache errors. I'll start with gateway logs.

alex: (paste) `kubectl -n prod logs deploy/inference-gateway --since=5m | grep -E "5.." | head -n 50`

alex: gateway logs show lots of upstream 502/504 and 500 with message "upstream error: model backend unavailable" and repeated `context deadline exceeded`.

maria: checking model-serving cluster: `kubectl -n models get pods -o wide | grep model-serve` shows several CrashLoopBackOffs on node gpu-5. OOMKilled on model-worker-47.

maria: metrics: model-worker-47 memory spiked before crash; pod was restarted and then traffic rebalanced causing other workers to overcommit.

samir: autoscaler logs show scale-up didn't trigger due to a bug in selector; scale-controller reported "no matching nodepool" after yesterday's tweak. Opening quick PR to revert.

alex: temporary mitigation: divert a fraction of traffic to fallback model (lower memory footprint) and enable circuit-breaker on long-running requests. Can someone flip the routing?

maria: I can flip routing in the runtime config. Pushing a safe traffic-split: 80% fallback-small-model, 20% primary. Applying: `rtctl routes set --service inference-gateway --split primary=20,fallback-small=80 --env prod`

incident-bot: Config change applied by maria at revision r5421. Observability: expect metric smoothing in ~30s.

alex: good. Also increase pod replica target for model-workers while we fix autoscaler: `kubectl scale deployment model-worker --replicas=10 -n models`

samir: manual scale applied. Note: if node shortage, pods will stay Pending. I'm standing up two on-demand GPU nodes in us-east-1 to relieve pressure.

ops-bot: New compute nodes booting: gpu-ondemand-xy1, gpu-ondemand-xy2 (us-east-1).

jin: product/customer note: any indications of user-facing failures? What percent of requests are returning 5xx for end users?

alex: checking SLO dashboards: user-facing 5xx for /v1/generate rose to 2.1% globally; estimated impacted requests ~ 1.4k/min. Most are retriable, but some customers with strict error handling see degraded UX.

jin: flagged to CSMs. I'll prepare a short status update: "We're investigating elevated error rate on generation API; mitigation in progress, traffic partially routed to fallback model, minimal data loss, ETA 30-60m". Will post to status.redwood.ai if we cross incident threshold.

maria: after traffic-split and scale, 5xx rate dropped to ~0.8% in 3 mins. Gateway latencies slightly up but error steady down.

alex: good improvement. Still seeing intermittent 500s from long requests (>10s). Enabling request timeouts/circuit-breaker to fail fast for slow calls: `gateway-config set --route /v1/generate --timeout 8s --circuit-breaker 50`

incident-bot: Gateway config changed by alex (timeout 8s, circuit-breaker threshold 50) at r5423.

samir: autoscaler revert PR merged; will redeploy scale-controller in 5m. That should restore autoscaling behavior.

maria: redeploying scale-controller now: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/scale-controller -n infra`

ops-bot: scale-controller rollout status: success.

alex: can we watch pending pods?

maria: pending pods are now scheduling onto on-demand nodes. Model-worker replicas increasing; memory usage stabilizing.

alex: 5xx rate down to 0.35% and trending down. Latency 95th still elevated but acceptable.

jin: thanks team. I'll hold off on public status page for now, will update CSMs. If we hit >1% again or sustained >15m, I'll post.

samir: follow-up actions noted: revert the autoscaler selector change in main branch with unit test, add canary for scale-controller changes, increase alert threshold hysteresis to avoid thundering.

alex: I'm going to prepare a short incident doc and handoff to next oncall in 30m. Who's on next shift?

samir: next oncall is jana (uk) starting at 18:00 UTC. I'll add her and @pagerduty-bot will page if we regress.

alex: handing off: current status: mitigation applied (traffic split + circuit-breaker + manual scale); autoscaler repaired and redeployed; 5xx rate back to normal. Ongoing tasks: monitor for 1h, follow up on root cause (OOM + autoscaler bug), postmortem owner: samir.

maria: I'll watch model cluster for 45m then hand off.

incident-bot: Handoff recorded. On-call shift change scheduled: alex -> jana at 18:00 UTC.

alex: thanks all. Quick notes for postmortem: collect heap dumps from model-worker-47, add memlimit guardrails, implement safe-traffic-split automation when pods restart, add alert to tie 5xx spike to autoscaler failures.

jin: I'll draft the customer impact note and coordinate with support for any escalations.

samir: I'll own the postmortem and remediation. Assigning tickets: INF-2314 (OOM investigation), INF-2315 (autoscaler selector fix), INF-2316 (alert hysteresis).

alex: closing thread for now, will reopen if regression. :thumbsup:
